summary.headline: Hero MotoCorp Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record ₹12,797 crores (+29% YoY) and EBITDA ₹1,856 crores (+31%), but management flagged a transitory margin hit from commodity inflation.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with ICE EBITDA margin up 100 bps YoY to 17%. Full-year FY26 revenue was ₹46,830 crores (+15%), EBITDA ₹6,871 crores (+17%) and PAT ₹5,268 crores (+14%). Commodity cost inflation starting March 2026 (₹2,000–2,100 per unit in Q4, offset by an equal revenue-per-unit increase) compressed gross margin by about 100 bps QoQ, and management expects a transitory margin impact in FY27. Management reiterated the 14–16% medium-term margin guidance but declined to commit to it for FY27 given the volatility.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 overall EBITDA margin (after ₹220 crore EV investment)

segments.name: India ICE business
segments.commentary: ICE EBITDA margin 17% in Q4 and FY26, driven by pricing, LEAP savings and operating leverage. Scooters grew 48% YoY; Destini capacity raised 50% and Xoom capacity being doubled.

segments.name: Electric (VIDA)
segments.commentary: EV scooter volumes 2.5x YoY; Q4 EV investment behind the business ₹220 crores. EBITDA loss per unit is declining each quarter per management. PLI now covers 3 products (~60% of portfolio), targeted to reach ~90%, worth ~13% of revenue as benefit.

segments.name: Global business
segments.commentary: Wholesale/dispatches grew 41% YoY, after 40% growth the prior year; present in 52 countries. Latin America is the main traction market; Africa launches planned for FY27.

segments.name: Harley-Davidson premium range
segments.commentary: Harley-Davidson range sales grew 26% YoY; X440T variant delivered 120% YoY growth in its launch quarter.

segments.name: Spare parts (PAM)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales ~₹6,200 crores (~+6%); management estimates ~50% of parts demand is currently served, with a second global parts centre in South India (₹700+ crores) to double parts handling capacity.

guidance_outlook: FY27 industry volume growth expected at high single digits, with scooters growing a couple of points faster than motorcycles; Hero expects to outgrow the industry in both.
Calibrated price increase of ~2% taken in April 2026 (₹700–₹3,500 per product); management says this does not fully cover the high-single-digit BOM cost increase.
Medium-term EBITDA margin guidance of 14–16% reiterated, but no FY27 commitment given; a transitory margin hit expected in the short term.
H1 FY27 growth expected to be stronger than H2 due to base effects; full-year growth momentum expected to continue.
Capex of over ₹1,500 crores committed for FY27, entirely in FY27, mainly for scooter and EV capacity.
Second EV capacity doubling expected before end of FY27; Xoom capacity doubling expected in the current quarter.
capex_capacity: EV capacity: expansion completed within about a month to reach ~50% above Q3 levels (~15,000 to ~25,000 units per month); a further doubling targeted before end of FY27. Management's ambition implies ~100,000 scooters/month.
ICE scooters: Destini capacity up 50%; Xoom capacity being doubled, expected to be complete this quarter.
Over ₹1,500 crores capex committed for FY27 for scooter and EV capacity expansion.
Second global parts centre in South India: over ₹700 crores, roughly doubling parts handling capacity.
Tirupati factory produces both ICE and EV scooters on separate lines within the same plant, sharing infrastructure.
demand_pricing: Dealer inventory around 5 weeks at the end of FY26, down from earlier in the year; EV scooter inventory in single-digit days nationally.
Retail growth outpaced dispatch growth in FY26, so channel stock fell and the company enters FY27 with healthier stock levels.
Post West Asia conflict, demand has not softened in April or the first week of May; the full cost inflation has not yet been passed to consumers.
Q4 average selling price up 3% QoQ across segments.
Management sees scooterization continuing (scooter share of industry up a couple of points each year) and says motorcycle demand is not being lost to scooters.
Retail market share has still declined arithmetically due to mix; management expects a reversal after a few more quarters of outgrowing the market in EV, scooters, exports and premium.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume outlook for motorcycles and scooters, and which models will drive growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry expects high-single-digit growth, with scooters growing a couple of points faster than motorcycles. Hero plans to outgrow the industry in both, with launches across commuter, high-displacement bikes and VIDA, though specifics were withheld.

qa_highlights.question: What is the quantum of the commodity and wage headwind, the price hikes taken, and the margin bridge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify given daily volatility. Price hike is ~2% of sale price, while BOM cost increases are in the high single digits. Offsets include BOM value engineering, LEAP savings, discretionary spend cuts and volume leverage, but these will not fully offset the impact in the short term.

qa_highlights.question: Have EV losses peaked, and how will PLI affect them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it is still in the EV build-out phase and that EBITDA loss per unit is falling each quarter. PLI covers 3 products (~60% of portfolio), targeted at ~90%, worth ~13% of revenue; BOM cost reduction is also a lever. EV revenue and loss figures were deferred offline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the recalibrated strategy three months into the CEO role?
qa_highlights.answer: Continue dominance in entry and commuter motorcycles (over 90% share in some ranges; 93% of talukas covered). Prioritise scooters, EVs (including Ather and Euler partnerships and VIDA), other low-emission powertrains such as higher-ethanol-blend vehicles, technology, and exports.

qa_highlights.question: How should exports and global business be viewed for the next 12–24 months, and what are the near-term risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is led by Latin America, with Africa launches planned for FY27 and Bangladesh coverage being extended. Fuel price increases in Bangladesh and Sri Lanka are weighing on demand short term, and freight costs are being passed to retail pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the half-yearly growth pattern for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 FY27 growth is expected to be stronger on base effects, with H2 relatively lower. Full-year growth momentum is expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin decline of over 100 bps QoQ in Q4 despite price hikes matching commodity costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Material cost inflation of ~₹2,100 per unit vs. ~₹2,000 revenue increase; the margin percentage impact came from unrecovered margin on that cost (about 60% of the decline), plus higher EV BOM costs. Aluminium, steel and rubber led the basket, and plastics rose on crude prices.

risks_watch: Commodity (aluminium, steel, rubber, plastics) and labour cost inflation since March 2026; ~2% price hike is far below the high-single-digit BOM increase, so the Q1 FY27 margin is at risk.
EV losses remain large during the build-out phase; PLI benefit of ~13% of revenue depends on coverage rising from ~60% to ~90%.
Retail market share has declined arithmetically despite category share gains; management says a reversal requires several more quarters of outperformance.
EPR (extended producer responsibility) regulation still evolving; pricing and possible retrospective impact unclear, and industry is working on operationalisation.
Mandatory ABS regulation: no development in recent months.
Fuel price increases and West Asia developments could dampen demand and raise freight costs in export markets such as Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, market share gains and the scooter/EV build-out, backed by specific numbers. Notably cautious and evasive on the FY27 margin: it declined to quantify commodity impact or commit to the 14–16% range for the full year, citing daily volatility.

So the price hike as of now does not cover fully the BOM cost increase.

growth.why: FY27 guided to high single-digit industry growth with Hero outgrowing it in both scooters and motorcycles, backed by >₹1,500 crore FY27 capex for scooter/EV capacity, Destini +50% and Xoom doubling, and a ~2% price increase, though no explicit company revenue growth number was given and the FY27 margin was not committed.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.why: EV capacity already lifted ~50% from ~15,000 to ~25,000 units/month, Destini ICE capacity up 50%, Xoom doubling due this quarter, and over Rs 1,500 crore FY27 capex committed for scooter/EV capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: H1 FY27 stronger than H2 on base effects; full year FY27
rows.why: Management guides high single-digit industry growth with Hero outgrowing in both scooters and motorcycles; FY26 scooters grew 48% and exports dispatched +41%, with dealer inventory at ~5 weeks.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex of over Rs 1,500 crore is already committed for FY27 and a second EV doubling is planned before FY27 end toward a ~100,000/month ambition, so further capex announcements are probable, though utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: BOM costs up high single digits versus a ~2% price hike and Q4 gross margin down over 100 bps QoQ; the Q1 FY27 margin is flagged at risk, though demand has not softened in April and early May.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans launches across commuter, high-displacement bikes and VIDA in FY27 and Africa launches, though specifics were withheld; X440T already grew 120% in its launch quarter.

rows.label: Commodity pass-through gap
rows.why: Only ~2% price increase taken in April 2026 against high single-digit BOM increases, so further price actions are needed to close the gap, but the company has not committed to them.

rows.label: Dividend and cash generation
rows.why: FY26 operating cash flow of Rs 9,395 crore (+80%) funded a record Rs 185/share dividend with a payout above 70%.

rows.label: EPR regulation impact
rows.why: EPR pricing and possible retrospective impact remain unclear with the industry still working on operationalisation, so the cost effect is unquantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, share gains and the EV and scooter capacity build-out, but cautious and evasive on FY27 margins, declining to quantify the commodity headwind or commit to 14-16% for the year; analysts pushed on margin bridge and EV losses.
